narrative.summary: BRICS has no permanent secretariat; its texts are adopted by leaders and ministers under a rotating presidency. At the Rio de Janeiro summit in July 2025, BRICS leaders adopted a dedicated statement on the global governance of AI, calling for UN-centred governance, national regulatory sovereignty, fair data governance and capacity building for developing countries.

instruments.official_title: BRICS Leaders' Statement on the Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: BRICS Leaders' Statement on the Global Governance of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Leaders' statement setting BRICS positions on AI governance. It calls for global AI governance strengthened through the United Nations, avoiding fragmentation and giving developing countries meaningful participation; affirms countries' right to set their own AI regulatory frameworks; seeks fair and inclusive data governance with respect for privacy, personal data and intellectual property; supports access to AI technology, finance, skills and infrastructure for developing countries, open-source and open science; and commits to address bias, misinformation, cybercrime and misuse with human oversight, transparency and accountability. It covers non-military uses of AI only.
instruments.current_status: Statement of BRICS leaders, published by the 2025 Brazilian BRICS presidency. The text describes itself as guidelines that BRICS countries remain open to revisiting.
instruments.evidence_reference: Text read on the Brazilian presidency site brics.br; the PDF has no printed date or place. File name suggests 6 July 2025 but URL dates are not used, so month only. Kept as a lead under the omnibus-declaration rule; needs review whether para 81 warrants a record.

membership_note: BRICS members as listed on the Indian presidency's official site (brics2026.gov.in, About BRICS, read 2026-10-26): Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Partner countries (Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan, Vietnam) are not members.

members_source.comment: Indian presidency site (brics2026.gov.in/about-us), read 2026-10-26: 'BRICS brings together eleven major emerging markets and developing countries' and lists Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and UAE under 'BRICS Member Countries'; 10 partner countries listed separately (Vietnam added to the earlier 9). Not changed: the Indian and Brazilian presidency pages list Saudi Arabia (SAU) as a member, but SAU stays out of members until its membership is confirmed (needs review).
